email.body1:
Randall, saw Nautilent rolled out Passkeys for agents and keeps doubling down on the top 500 brokerages.

Selling into a tight, named set of large brokerages means every account matters, and there are usually more of them in-market than the team can personally cover. Our AI SDR researches, writes, and follows up on its own, so coverage scales without new headcount: 3-5x more meetings per rep.

I built a signal play for Nautilent off your hiring and tech-stack signals, and accounts showing them tend to progress about 4.4x faster. Worth 15 minutes for me to walk you through it?
email.body2:
Randall, quick follow-up for Nautilent.

With a finite list of enterprise brokerages, the question is not lead volume, it is how many of the right meetings you need to book to hit target. Most teams cannot answer that cleanly, so the gap shows up late in the quarter.

Want to grab 15 minutes? I will walk you through our pipeline model and show exactly how many meetings Nautilent needs to close that gap, and where the math breaks if you only add reps.
email.body3:
Randall, last bit of proof for Nautilent.

Memgraph had more in-market accounts than the team could touch and could not hire SDRs fast enough. They ran our AI SDR to $2.7M in pipeline, 600 replies, and 60 BANT-qualified deals in 90 days, same team, live in four weeks, every email auto-logged to their CRM.

I pulled a benchmark of how Nautilent's reply rate likely compares to other niche B2B platforms. Want to hop on a quick call and I will walk you through it?
email.body4:
Randall, I will stop reaching out on this one, but did not want to leave you empty-handed.

If scaling pipeline without adding headcount is not a priority this quarter, no problem at all. Running both business development and marketing is its own kind of busy, and timing matters.

Before I close your file, worth 15 minutes to walk through a one-page playbook of three AI-SDR plays scoped to your brokerage motion? I will tailor it to Nautilent either way.
